newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: Brazil asks for delay of Mercosur meeting.
newsitem.headline: Brazil asks for delay of Mercosur meeting.

text.p: Brazil has asked for a delay of a Mercosur customs union meeting of economy ministers and central bank presidents scheduled for Thursday, a Paraguayan government official said Wednesday.

"The meeting was scheduled and we were working on the organization of the meeting, but late Tuesday we received the order to suspend the work...the meeting is now fixed for June 18," Anibal Reyes, integration director at Paraguay's Economy Ministry, told Reuters.

Sources from Paraguay's central bank said that Paraguay had received a request for a delay from Brazil to be able to respond to calls from its Mercosur partners for changes to Brazilian import financing rules adopted in April.
Paraguay is currently heading the revolving presidency of Mercosur, which groups it with Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay.

The meeting's new date of June 18 coincides with the annual Mercosur meeting of economy and foreign ministers. But the central bank sources said work for a solution to the disagreement over Brazil's import financing rules is likely to continue into July.
Brazil at the beginning of April imposed tougher limits on importers using financing of 360 days or less.
Brazil agreed to put the new rules on hold until the end of July for its Mercosur partners after accusations of protectionism from Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay.
